help.title: How ShopWiz works
help.hint: New here? Tap (?) for a short guide.
help.start.title: Getting started
help.start.body:
A list lives behind a 10-character ID like K7QM-2XPA-9F. Whoever knows it can see and edit the lists – no account needed.
Share the ID with ⤴: QR code, share menu or link. Opening the link is all it takes to join.
Your device remembers the ID. Settings ⚙ → “Forget ID on this device” removes it from this device only.
Your device name is what others see. Change it any time in Settings ⚙ → “This device”.
Pick the look under Settings ⚙ → “Appearance”: Dark, AMOLED (true black, easy on OLED screens), Sunset (dark plum and coral), Light, Mint (soft mint and green) or Mango (bright and fruity). Until you pick one, ShopWiz follows your browser's light/dark setting.
The text size (small, normal, large) is set per device under Settings ⚙ → “This device”.
help.add.title: Adding items
help.add.body:
Type into the field at the bottom and press Enter or ＋.
Amounts are recognised: “2 milk”, “500g minced meat”, “milk x2”.
While typing, things you added before are suggested – tap one to add it.
Paste several lines at once (e.g. from a chat) to add several items.
If an item is already on the list, ShopWiz asks whether to increase the amount instead.
A long press on the yellow + button opens “New item”: amount, priority, note, group and list at once – “Another” keeps the dialog open for the next one. With the installed app this also works right from the app icon: long press → “Add item”.
help.check.title: Checking off & inactive items
help.check.body:
Tap an item to check it off; tap again to undo. Checked items move to the end of their group.
On a phone you can swipe, too: one way checks off, the other moves the item to “Inactive”. Which way does what (or whether swiping is off) is set under Settings ⚙ → “Swipe”.
The eye 👁 next to “I'm shopping” hides checked items – handy in the shop. It only applies to this device.
Focus mode (the four corners next to the eye) shows nothing but the list: categories and items to check off, large and black on white or white on black depending on the skin. Check off by tapping or – if turned on – by swiping. The bar at the very top, “Leave focus mode”, takes you back; to its right the eye hides checked items and the phone symbol keeps the screen on.
When everything is checked, “Finish shopping” appears: checked items move to “Inactive”, you are checked out and the screen may turn off again.
“Move checked to inactive” clears the list at any time – the items wait under “Inactive items” at the bottom.
Tap an inactive item to put it back on the list, with its group, amount and note.
The ⋯ next to an item opens its details: name, amount, note, group, who added it, delete.
Almost everything can be undone right away with “Undo”.
help.groups.title: Groups
help.groups.body:
Groups sort the list, e.g. along your way through the shop: Bakery, Fridge, Drinks.
“Add group” creates one; the next item you type goes straight into it.
Move items by dragging the handle ⋮⋮ or via ⋯ → Group. ＋ on a group adds directly to it.
ShopWiz learns: an item you put into a group lands there automatically next time.
Groups without items wait under “Inactive items” until an item comes back.
help.shop.title: Shopping together
help.shop.body:
🛒 “I'm shopping” shows the others that you are in the shop – and where (the group of the item you checked last).
As soon as someone else is in the shop too, 📍 “Call” appears: “Where are you?”, “Come to me”, “Meet at the checkout”, “I'm done”. The other phone vibrates; one tap answers.
If a phone is off or offline, the signal arrives as soon as ShopWiz is open there again. The phone symbol next to it keeps the screen on.
Once the last item is checked, “Finish shopping” ends the trip. After 60 minutes without activity you are checked out automatically anyway.
In focus mode, “Aa” at the top sets the text size for the focus mode only.
help.lists.title: Several lists & shop address
help.lists.body:
Tap the list name at the top to switch lists or create a new one.
The magnifier 🔍 next to the list name searches the list – notes, translations and “Inactive items” included.
⋯ next to the list name opens the list options: rename, address, groups, share as text, history, backup.
“Share as text” sends the open items, one per line, to a chat or a note – also available under ⤴ Share.
With a shop address, a navigation button appears next to the list name.
Several IDs on one device? Settings ⚙ → “Switch”.
Select text on a web page or in a note → Share → ShopWiz: every line becomes an item of the list opened last (installed app, Android).
help.offline.title: Offline & simultaneous changes
help.offline.body:
The dot at the top is green when everything is synced and orange while offline or syncing.
Without a connection you can keep working; changes are sent as soon as you are back online.
If two people changed the same thing at the same time, a notice appears and anyone can pick the right value.
help.backup.title: Backup & import
help.backup.body:
Settings ⚙ → “Backup & import” downloads your lists as a text file (Markdown) – with groups, amounts, notes, priority, address, travel mode and translations.
You can edit it in any text editor and import it again – into the same ID (no duplicates) or as a new ID.
A simple list with one item per line works too, also from the start screen.
help.privacy.title: Privacy
help.privacy.body:
No account, no cookies, no tracking, no advertising.
Stored are only your lists, the names you enter and timestamps.
An ID is deleted after a long time without use (adjustable in the settings), inactive devices after 30 days.
Anyone with the ID can see the lists – only share it with people you trust. “Renew ID” locks out old links.

help.travel.title: Travel mode
help.travel.body:
Shopping abroad? Turn on “Travel mode” in the list menu (⋯ next to the list name). The country comes from the shop address, or you pick it.
Under each item its translation appears with the country's flag. Tap it to show it big to the staff – swipe to the next item.
“Translate N items” translates everything at once; single items can be translated or corrected in the item details. Translations are remembered for the whole ID.

help.prio.title: Priority
help.prio.body:
Mark items in their details: ↑ Important (“don't come home without it”) or ↓ Not important (“never mind if you can't find it”). Important items go to the top of their group, unimportant ones to the bottom.
When adding, the small button next to the group picks the importance of the next item. With “Shortcuts ! and ?” turned on in the list menu, typing “!Diapers” or “? Basil” does the same – the mark is not saved in the name.
How the mark looks (in the box, on its corner or before the name) is chosen per device in the settings.

help.ai.title: AI assistants
help.ai.body:
Claude, ChatGPT, Grok or Siri can read your lists and – if you allow it – add, check off and change items. For example: “Put milk and 200 g minced meat on the shopping list.”
Groups and travel mode, too: “Sort the list by the aisles of the supermarket” creates groups, orders them, moves the items and sorts them within the groups. “I'm shopping in Italy, translate everything” turns on travel mode and writes the translations – often better than the machine translation, which never overwrites them.
Assistants know “Inactive”, too: “What else do we usually buy?” reads the inactive items, “Put the pizza back on the list” brings it back with group and amount, “Take the candles off” moves them there, “Remember baking powder for later” puts it straight there.
Settings ⚙ → “AI assistants” → pick the assistant → “Connect”. You get an address with a secret key, shown only once, and short steps for that assistant.
Each assistant shows up as a participant of its own; what it changes is in the history. Remove it any time in the settings or under participants.
“Assistants may change lists” is the switch for write access – off means read only. “Renew ID” disconnects all assistants.
The assistant's provider sees the lists when you ask it about them.

help.link.title: List groups
help.link.body:
Several shops that sell similar things? In the list menu under “List group”, tick the other lists. Linked lists share their items: what is on one is on all of them.
A shared item is checked off once – wherever. In the other shops it is checked, too, with a green “bought at Lidl” label. Groups and order stay per shop.
The green “Group” button when adding sends the next item to every linked list; tap it = only this list. The default is set per device in the settings. “Also at …” / “In the whole group” in the item details changes it later.
A list that leaves the group keeps its own copy of the shared items.
